 By BVM Sportsdesk, 7h ago Injury concerns and roster shortages are shaping the Pacific Division’s early season. Sacramento ’s Keegan Murray is still dealing with stiffness in his surgically repaired ankle, while short-handed Golden State has found bright spots in rookie Yaxel Lendeborg and its supporting cast. Phoenix two-way player Drew Timme says he’s focused on proving his impact goes beyond conventional measurements.
 By the Numbers Murray: 7 points, 3 rebounds and 1 steal per game through 2 games.
 Lendeborg: 18.7 points, 8.4 rebounds and 4.3 assists per game through 3 appearances.
 Against Phoenix, Lendeborg scored a career-high 26 points; De’Anthony Melton added 25 on 8-of-13 shooting.
 Warriors centers Graham Ike and Charles Bassey combined for 22 points and 17 rebounds in 36 minutes.
 Yes, But Golden State has lost three straight, and its latest defeat came while the team was shorthanded. Coach Steve Kerr sees the performance as evidence the Warriors can compete when players are connected, but Lendeborg’s expected heavy rookie workload could test him over the season.
 State of Play Murray is listed as questionable for Sunday’s game against Memphis because of left ankle capsulitis.
 Kerr expects Lendeborg to shoulder a major role, potentially leading the Warriors in minutes this season.
 Timme is on a two-way contract with Phoenix and is seeking a place in the NBA despite what he sees as a mismatch with conventional player expectations.
 Bottom Line Early-season opportunity is meeting uncertainty: Sacramento needs Murray healthy, while Golden State is leaning on its depth and a rookie expected to play extensively. Phoenix’s Timme is making the case that basketball value isn’t always obvious on paper.
